Activity data covers roughly 35 hours through July 31 at 10:00.

The seasonal campaign spent $22.54 across 16,922 impressions with 10 link clicks and 116 engagements. The offer campaign spent $25.49 across 16,416 impressions with 11 clicks. The four posts averaged $12.34 in spend per post. The price post led with 6 clicks and a 0.081% CTR. The wall post had the highest CPC at $2.06.

Combined spend across both campaigns reached roughly $48.03 with 21 clicks and 33,338 impressions.

The average CPC of about $2.29 is steep for a $400 budget. That rate would yield only around 175 link clicks over the full flight.

The billing model appears to charge per engagement rather than per click. The 116 engagements cost more than the 10 link clicks suggest.

The campaign is set to pay by link click, yet billed engagements far exceed actual clicks. This suggests Twitter may be counting likes or other interactions as billable events for this objective. Normally, billed engagements should equal link clicks.
